text: Hey, good afternoon everybody. Danny Jones here from the Goose Hummock Shops with this week's fishing report. You got Labor Day weekend coming up. I did jot down a few things here so I can make sure I cover everything. If you're coming for the weekend, to give you a little insight if you're going to be trying to fish here this weekend. So, let me begin with inshore. The bonito are the big story right now. They're spread out through Buzzards Bay, the south side and pushing towards the canal as well. The albies are starting to show, still scattered though. Very spotty, but this it's starting. There's plenty of small bait around including some silver sides and chovies and herring as well. Have some epoxy jigs, tins, metals and albie snacks ready to go pre-rigged. We have all that here at the store. Stripers in the canal, it's been up and down as well. The canal is getting interesting again. You got cooler water temps. There's stripers, bonito and cocktail blues all all around there with plenty of bait in the water as well. If you get a chance, you can always hit the canal when you're coming on Cape. First light and the tide changes are the windows that I'd be watching. Always once again, early morning, later in the evenings best as well. And Cape Cod Bay is also been holding some stripers and bigger blue fish with squid and peanut bunker around. There's also some big tuna fish in the bay as well if that's going to be your game. The weather doesn't look that great this weekend, but try to get out there if you can. On the surf side, Nauset's been fishing a little bit better. I talked to a customer today. They had a few fish last night. Nothing that big in a 27 to 30-in class, but it's still action. The stripers are also being caught along Cape Cod Bay and the backside beaches and the outer Cape is starting to show more potential as well. Once again, you want some pencil poppers, looking for birds and bait, tins, epoxy jigs and soft plastics ready. Ron-Z's and the such like that. On the offshore scene, that can that's getting better. I talked to Phil the other day. There is some wreck fish back at the sword, but it's been spotty as well. But definitely worth watching. There's plenty of sand eels around, plenty of dolphins out there, the whales are still there. There's a lot of life, so there's still fish there. So, if you're tuna fishing, the sword's probably going to be your best bet. Always and always check your current tuna regulations as well before heading out. The fresh water. Now, this is going to get better and better each day now. With fall coming, it's getting darker at night, the water the pond temperature is going to start to drop. Stocking for trout usually starts October 1st. They usually do it for the first 2 weeks and you need all the ponds they usually hit. Nickerson State Park, Baker's Pond, Crystal Lake, Herring Pond and the such. So, but that's not going to start till early October, but there's still trout around. The largemouth bass fishing and the chain pickerel fishing has been very good. My good friend Captain Rich was out the other day. He fished one of the local ponds here and he did very good with largemouth. He had fish up to 5 lb in his little boat. So, he had a great day just with soft plastics, Yamamoto Senkos and things like that. So, my Labor Day takeaway is there's a lot of things to do. Weather's going to be permitting, but there's with the bonito around, albies are starting to show. Canal's coming back. Stripers are getting active and the tuna are still on the radar offshore and the fresh water bite is starting to get better and better each and every day. So, there's plenty to do this weekend. If you're coming down the Cape, stop in. We'll get you geared up, we'll get you out there and hopefully you can catch some fish this weekend. Happy Labor Day everybody.
